    - heading "Quantum hardware technologies" [level=2]
    - heading "Gate-based superconducting processors" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Superconducting qubits are built with superconducting electric circuits operating at cryogenic temperature. Amazon Braket provides access to quantum hardware based on superconducting qubits from IQM, and Rigetti.
    - paragraph:
      - link "Learn more about IQM gate-based superconducting processors":
        - /url: /braket/quantum-computers/iqm/
    - paragraph:
      - link "Learn more about Rigetti gate-based superconducting processors":
        - /url: /braket/quantum-computers/rigetti/
    - heading "Gate-based ion-trap processors" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Trapped-ion quantum computers implement qubits using electronic states of charged atoms called ions. The ions are confined and suspended in free space using electromagnetic fields. Amazon Braket provides access to ion-trap quantum computers from AQT and IonQ.
    - paragraph:
      - link "Learn more about AQT gate-based ion-trap processors":
        - /url: /braket/quantum-computers/aqt/
    - paragraph:
      - link "Learn more about IonQ gate-based ion-trap processors":
        - /url: /braket/quantum-computers/ionq/
    - paragraph
    - heading "Neutral atom-based quantum processors" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Rydberg atom-based quantum computers take advantage of long-range van der Waals interactions between neutral atoms arranged in one, two or three-dimensional arrays that can be addressed to simulate quantum systems of interest, beyond the capabilities of current classical computers. Amazon Braket provides access to Rydberg atom-based quantum computers from QuEra Computing.
    - paragraph:
      - link "Learn more about QuEra Rydberg atom-based processors":
        - /url: /braket/quantum-computers/quera/
